tasks.short: Prepare purchase orders and employee expense reports, obtain approvals, and transfer approved records.

steps.what: Collect purchase requests and chase missing supplier, quantity, cost-centre and delivery details.
Read supplier quotes and identify prices, quantities, delivery terms and reference numbers.

loop.input: Supplier quote and complete purchase request.
loop.output: Quote details with source references and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate supplier identity, currency, quantities and arithmetic; compare requested items; clerk confirms ambiguous terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry per quote; missing or conflicting fields go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier quote layouts and delivery terms vary. Structured quotes bypass extraction.

steps.what: Enter purchase-order lines, coding and delivery details in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Approve the purchase commitment against budget, need and delegated authority.
Send the approved purchase order to the supplier and retain its reference.
Read employee receipts and supporting expense explanations.

loop.input: Expense receipt and employee expense explanation.
loop.output: Expense details with receipt references and missing-field flags.
loop.check: Check date, currency, totals and duplicate receipts; validate tax fields against configured rules.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per receipt; unreadable receipts and uncertain tax treatment go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Receipt images and explanations vary. Structured card transactions use direct imports.

steps.what: Compile expense lines, attach receipts and apply policy and cost-centre codes in the {EXPENSE}.
Approve business purpose and decide documented expense-policy exceptions.
Transfer approved expense reports to the {ERP} and check import totals.

tasks.design: Configure intake, mandatory fields, approval routing and order generation in the {PROCUREMENT}, with receipt capture and policy checks in the {EXPENSE}. Bounded extraction loops handle variable documents; approved records pass to the {ERP} through a configured connector with duplicate protection and control totals. Supplier dispatch requires an approved, unchanged purchase order; payment release remains a separate action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variable documents, incomplete requests and disconnected approval records made setup and maintenance costly. Existing features were often available but incompletely configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Current capture tools handle variable documents, while configuration and small connectors handle most routing and arithmetic. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector development effort without changing approval responsibilities.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier master errors, mixed tax treatment and undocumented business purpose still require investigation. National expense and consultation rules vary.
tasks.human_edge: People establish business purpose, challenge unnecessary commitments and decide justified policy exceptions.

ambition.what: Receipt-based expense submission support for field staff without regular desktop access.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time retyping and more time resolving incomplete or disputed claims. With delegated authority, they can return incomplete submissions directly; spending and exception approvals stay with the relevant manager.

reach.task: Review outstanding purchase commitments against remaining budgets.
reach.learn: Commitment accounting, budget ownership and the difference between ordered, received and invoiced spend.

evidence.claim: Ramp documents a US case replacing manual quote-PDF entry into purchase orders; transfer to this setting needs validation.
AFAS Profit documents invoice extraction and supplier identification; this supports document capture, not proven expense-receipt accuracy.
The cited survey found substantial paper or email invoice approval, supporting mailbox handoffs as a plausible prior.
Purchase-order generation, expense policy checks and approval routing generally use existing configuration.

assumptions: The task covers preparation and approval routing, not payment release.
The {PROCUREMENT} and {EXPENSE} support configurable approvals and an existing {ERP} connector.
Time shares cover both purchase-order and expense-report work, including approval handoffs.
Build ranges are planning estimates for one entity and a limited document set; remaining-time estimates need a pilot.
GDPR applies to employee expense data. National rules may require consultation when processing or access arrangements change.
unknowns: Actual volume split between purchase orders and expense reports.
Available connector licences and approved access scopes.
Share of structured quotes, card transactions and unreadable receipts.
Approval thresholds, tax jurisdictions and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which intake and connector functions can be enabled without custom code?
Which receipt fields and quote terms fail validation on a representative sample?
new_work: Review uncertain document fields and tax exceptions.
Maintain supplier, cost-centre and approval mappings.
Investigate failed imports and duplicate dispatch attempts.
Periodically check capture quality and access permissions.

tasks.short: Prepare a trial balance, investigate discrepancies and produce an approved period snapshot.

steps.what: Select the entity, period and ledger scope and run the {ERP} trial balance.
Export balances and arrange the working trial balance in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Check debit-credit equality, opening balances, control accounts and unusual account balances.
Investigate exceptions with supporting records and propose accounting corrections.
Approve correction amounts, accounts, dates and supporting evidence.
Post approved corrections and rerun the trial balance in the {ERP}.
Review unresolved items and approve the trial-balance snapshot for period reporting.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} trial balance, comparison checks and correction approval workflow, removing the duplicate working file in the {SPREADSHEET}. Link exceptions to journals and supporting records in the {DOCS}, then regenerate a versioned snapshot after approved corrections. No model loop is needed for arithmetic, comparisons or posting approved journals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Working files compensated for poorly configured reports and fragmented supporting evidence. Accounting policy and correction approval could not be replaced by arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and journal workflows cover most of the task. Configuration and small extensions are cheaper to implement and test with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Balanced debits and credits do not prove correct classification, completeness or period allocation. Missing transactions and unsupported journals still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk traces discrepancies to real transactions; the accountant decides the accounting treatment and accepts unresolved items.

ambition.what: Daily escalation decisions for unreconciled control-account balances.

tasks.altitude: The clerk works from linked exceptions instead of rebuilding a workbook. With delegated escalation limits, they can seek correction earlier; journal approval and period sign-off remain with the accountant.

reach.task: Prepare control-account reconciliations and explain unresolved differences.
reach.learn: Cut-off, accruals, suspense accounts and reconciliation evidence.

evidence.claim: Trial-balance arithmetic, report scheduling and approved journal posting generally fit existing financial-system configuration.
Debit-credit equality cannot establish transaction completeness, correct classification or correct cut-off.

assumptions: A single {ERP} holds the entity's general ledger and relevant subledgers.
The working {SPREADSHEET} duplicates reporting functions rather than providing essential consolidation logic.
Correction and sign-off steps are conditional; shares represent average effort across reporting cycles.
Build and remaining-time ranges are estimates, not results from the digest.
GDPR applies to personal data in journal support; this design does not introduce employee monitoring.
unknowns: Existing report, reconciliation and journal-approval capabilities.
Number of entities, currencies and separate ledgers.
Whether workbook adjustments are posted back to the ledger.
Actual exception rate and correction authority.
research_questions: Can the existing report replace every essential working-file calculation?
Which control accounts can be checked automatically against authoritative subledger totals?
new_work: Maintain account mappings and exception thresholds.
Check scheduled reports for stale periods or incomplete imports.
Review unresolved exceptions and failed journal postings.
Verify that approved snapshots remain reproducible after later postings.

tasks.short: Compile financial and audit tables, reconcile them to source records, and distribute approved reports.

steps.what: Extract cash, expenditure, receivables, payables and ledger reports from the {ERP}.
Combine extracts and map accounts, periods and cost centres in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Reconcile report totals to ledger balances and investigate missing or duplicated rows.
Populate financial tables and charts in the standard report document.
Draft short explanations of material movements and unresolved reporting limitations.

loop.input: Validated tables, report exceptions and approved variance explanations.
loop.output: Draft commentary with references to every figure and supplied explanation.
loop.check: Check every number against table cells; reject unsupported causes and omitted material exceptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt per report; failed checks leave blank commentary for the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Arithmetic is deterministic, but concise wording varies with the supplied explanations. Fixed sections use templates.

steps.what: Review figures, commentary, limitations and recipient suitability before approving release.
Distribute the approved report internally and archive its source version.

tasks.design: Use scheduled {ERP} extracts and deterministic transformations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to create reconciled datasets, then generate standard tables in the {DOCS} and views in the {BI}. A bounded loop drafts commentary only from validated figures and approved explanations. The {WORKFLOW} records release approval and distributes the approved version to authorised internal recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Report definitions, mappings and source cut-offs lived in individual workbooks. Connecting them into a reproducible process required development and agreement on definitions.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled exports, governed datasets and document templates are mature. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of transformations and report generators; bounded drafting reduces writing effort.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting definitions, late postings and explaining why a result changed remain difficult. A numerically correct report can still mislead through scope or presentation.
tasks.human_edge: People decide materiality, distinguish an observed movement from its cause and explain limitations to decision-makers.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on which overdue receivable groups need collector review.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more of the week testing definitions and investigating movements. With delegated thresholds, they can refer ageing exceptions to collectors; accountants retain report-release authority.

reach.task: Maintain a reconciled finance dataset and its report definitions.
reach.learn: Data modelling, source lineage, refresh controls and access rules.

reach.task: Investigate material expenditure movements by cost centre.
reach.learn: Variance analysis and how to obtain evidence for business explanations.

evidence.claim: Structured financial extracts, account mappings, reconciliations and report templates support deterministic report generation.
A bounded drafting loop can use supplied explanations, but accounting interpretation still requires review.

assumptions: Scope is recurring internal reporting, not statutory filing or an audit opinion.
Existing {ERP} reports are used directly where they already meet the requirement.
The baseline includes a short commentary section; otherwise s5 can be eliminated.
Build estimates cover one report family with agreed definitions; time savings require pilot measurement.
GDPR applies to personal data in reports. Access is aggregated where individual detail is unnecessary.
unknowns: Number of reports, entities and source systems.
Which reports already run adequately in the {ERP} or {BI}.
Whether account and cost-centre definitions are agreed.
Permitted recipients, data granularity and refresh frequency.
research_questions: Which manual reports can be retired or replaced by existing views?
Can every published total be traced to a frozen source extract?
Does commentary drafting save review time on representative reports?
new_work: Maintain report definitions, mappings and templates.
Handle failed refreshes and reconciliation exceptions.
Audit recipient access and preserve reproducible report versions.

tasks.short: Maintain financial inventory records, reconcile stock movements and process approved adjustments.

steps.what: Retrieve receipts, issues, returns and count records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Record stock movements and their financial values in the {ERP}.
Compare quantities and values across stock records, count results and the general ledger.
Recount disputed stock and check physical locations and condition.
Resolve timing, unit, damage and missing-movement differences with the warehouse team.
Approve stock adjustments or valuation changes against evidence and delegated limits.
Post approved adjustments and retain the reconciled inventory record.

tasks.design: Connect movement records from the {OPS_SYSTEM} to the {ERP}, using unique transaction identifiers, unit mappings and the approved valuation policy. Deterministic reconciliations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} create an exception queue in the {WORKFLOW}; warehouse staff verify physical differences and accountants approve adjustments. Approved changes post once, with a linked audit trail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate stock and finance records used inconsistent item identifiers, units and cut-offs. Physical discrepancies could not be resolved through a records interface.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing movement exports and financial import interfaces support reliable synchronisation. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mapping, replay and reconciliation controls.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded physical movements, damaged goods, disputed counts and valuation judgement remain difficult. Integration cannot prove stock exists or is saleable.
tasks.human_edge: Warehouse staff establish physical facts; the clerk resolves operational context and the accountant decides financial treatment.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on which stock variances need a targeted recount.

tasks.altitude: The clerk replaces duplicate posting with investigation of stock-to-ledger differences. With delegated thresholds, they can request targeted recounts; valuation and write-off authority remain with the accountant.

reach.task: Assess how recurring scrap and unit-conversion differences affect standard costs.
reach.learn: Units of measure, standard costing, scrap treatment and evidence from operations.

reach.task: Prepare inventory-to-ledger reconciliations and support valuation adjustments.
reach.learn: Inventory valuation, cut-off and the distinction between quantity and value corrections.

evidence.claim: Inventory movement imports, unit conversions and ledger reconciliations are structured deterministic processes.
Physical counts and condition checks cannot be established by synchronising accounting records alone.

assumptions: This task applies to a company holding material physical inventory.
The baseline has separate operational and financial records; an already integrated installation needs configuration only.
Routine valuation follows an approved policy; discretionary write-offs require approval.
Shares average recurring record maintenance and conditional recounts, rather than requiring a recount for every movement.
Build and remaining-time estimates require validation against interfaces and exception samples.
GDPR applies where records identify staff; individual performance monitoring is outside this design.
unknowns: Whether stock movements already post automatically to the {ERP}.
Item identifiers, units, valuation methods and cut-off conventions.
Availability of immutable movement identifiers and correction events.
Count frequency, discrepancy rate and adjustment authority.
research_questions: Can source movements be replayed without duplicate financial postings?
Which differences reflect timing rather than genuine stock loss?
Can existing inventory configuration replace the proposed custom integration?
new_work: Monitor missing, duplicate and out-of-order movement events.
Investigate stock-to-ledger exceptions and arrange recounts.
Check approved adjustments and reconciliation evidence.

role.altitude: The week shifts from rekeying and assembling files toward resolving exceptions, checking evidence and preparing decisions. New rights require explicit delegation: the clerk can request missing evidence, escalate control failures and initiate recounts within agreed limits.
reach: Accountant: prepare reconciliations and evidence-backed correction requests.
Budget analyst: analyse purchase commitments and expenditure movements.
Business intelligence analyst: maintain reproducible finance datasets.
Cost estimator: investigate recurring stock and unit-cost differences.
skills_to_grow: Data mappings, interface controls and duplicate prevention.
Reviewing extracted fields and source-linked commentary.
GDPR, applicable national rules and AI literacy for bounded model use.
role.ambitious_version: Become the finance team's first-line exception analyst, connecting purchasing, expenses, ledger reporting and stock records into timely, evidence-backed escalation decisions.
